caption text: Figure 1. The methods of section 4 mapped by the question each answers, in the four purposes of section 7 (columns). Each method has one mark, placed at the purpose where the author's matrix (Table 9, with the failure-frame column named in its note) rates it highest and fewest other methods share that rating; the author's model is rated well suited to all four and sits where it has no other well-suited method beside it. Italic names are not rated in Table 9 and are placed from their description in section 4. Mark shape shows whether the method gives a people count directly, only by a further step, or not at all; orange is the author's model. Built from `analysis/method_tests_2025/method_catalogue.csv` (Table 2).
message: Methods answer different questions, and the ones that give a people count directly are not the ones that serve every purpose.

caption text: Figure 2. Each method's reading of Australia on the common 2021 to 2023 data, as run and under lines (a), (b) and (c) of section 5.11, beside the model's widened ranges (million people, log scale). Every reading is one dot, 19 readings of five methods on each line, including the footprint's pasture-only readings; the footprint's printed range in Table 5 leaves those out. Line (a) keeps the productivity basis as part of the method, line (b) treats it as an input, and line (c) adds one per-person requirement and waste treatment to line (b) (cell c1 of Table S7). The grey band is the corrected release's 5th to 95th percentile (31.1 to 49.2) and the hatched band the improved release's (37.9 to 60.0); the vertical lines mark each release's base value. Built from `harmonised_comparison_lines.csv`, `harmonised_line_c.csv`, `results/ranges_2025-fixed_wide.csv` and `results/ranges_2025-improved_wide.csv`.
message: As run, every aggregate method reads well above the model's ranges, and the footprint and HALF come down toward them only when productivity is counted as an input (line b).

caption text: Figure 3. The factor by which each single choice moved the answer of the author's model, one at a time (Table 8, panel A; higher capacity over lower, log scale). Single choices are ranked by factor; the drought allowance appears twice, with the weather factor on every yield (2.19) and on crop output alone (1.03), joined by the bracket. Below the line, not ranked: the diet C upper bound (triangle), two bundles of settings (squares) and the spread across the settings drawn together (diamonds). Built from `analysis/method_tests_2025/design_choices_panels.csv`.
message: The weather allowance moves the model by 2.19 on every yield but only 1.03 on crops alone, and diet, the unit and the allowance outrank waste and land.
